name: Soyuz TM-31
payload: Expedition 1: William Shepherd (NASA, commander), Yuri Gidzenko (Soyuz commander) and Sergei Krikalev (flight engineer)
first: Carried the first long-duration crew to the International Space Station
description: Soyuz TM-31 carried Expedition 1, the first long-duration crew of the International Space Station: NASA's William Shepherd as commander, Yuri Gidzenko as Soyuz commander and Sergei Krikalev as flight engineer. A Soyuz-U lifted off from Baikonur Site 1/5 on 2000-10-31 at 07:52:47 UTC. On 2000-11-02 at 09:21:40 UTC the ship docked, fully automatically with the Kurs system, at the aft port of the Zvezda module (Wikipedia and spacefacts give 09:21:03). The Russian mission-control report has it hovering 150 m from the port at 09:12:12 UTC. The hatch was opened at 10:23 UTC. The crew stayed 136 days 14 hours 7 minutes and went home on Space Shuttle STS-102, landing on 2001-03-21, not in this Soyuz. Soyuz TM-31 stayed docked until 2001-05-06, when it undocked at 02:21:09 UTC and landed in Kazakhstan at 05:41:28 UTC with the visiting crew of Soyuz TM-32: Talgat Musabayev, Yuri Baturin and Dennis Tito.

events.label: DOCKING
events.note: Docks automatically with the Kurs system at the aft port of Zvezda at 09:21:40 UTC on 2000-11-02, after hovering 150 m out at 09:12:12 UTC; Wikipedia gives 09:21:03.

events.label: HATCH OPEN
events.note: The crew opens the hatch at 10:23 UTC (ESA); the mission-control report quotes Krikalev's hatch-open report at 10:46 to 10:52 UTC.

events.label: UNDOCKING
events.note: Undocks from Zvezda at 02:21:09 UTC on 2001-05-06; the Expedition 1 crew had gone home on STS-102 on 2001-03-21.

events.label: LANDING
events.note: Lands at 05:41:28 UTC on 2001-05-06 in Kazakhstan, near Arkalyk, with Musabayev, Baturin and Tito, after 186 days 21 hours 48 minutes.
